app.noPersonalData: This page does not collect sign-ups, location, or phone numbers.
app.notLegalAdvice: If you are in danger, call 112. This is crime-prevention information, not legal advice.

home.title: Stay safe in Korea
home.subtitle: Crime prevention guide for international students
home.knowTitle: Three things police want you to know
home.know1: Prosecutors, police, and banks never ask you to move money to a “safe account” by phone.
home.know2: A part-time job that pays a lot for simple errands can be a crime.
home.know3: Never lend your bank account or card — not even to a friend.
home.checkDesc: If someone asked you to do this, check now
home.jobsTitle: Wait — this may not be a part-time job
home.jobsDesc: You can become a suspect, not only a victim
home.showDesc: Use Korean sentences if you cannot explain
home.reportDesc: Call 112. You can ask for an interpreter
home.embassyDesc: Call 112 first in danger. Your embassy helps with passports and detention

check.title: 30-second danger check
check.lead: If any answer is YES, stop. Do not send money, move items, or lend your account.
check.stopBody: This is not a part-time job. Stop sending money, delivering cash, lending accounts, or installing apps. Call 112.
check.okBody: No danger signal right now. Still refuse high-pay errands, account lending, and unknown parcels.

q.money: Is someone telling you to send money?
q.account: Are they asking to borrow your account or debit card?
q.cash: Are they asking you to receive cash and pass it to someone else?
q.parcel: Are they asking you to carry a stranger’s package?
q.police-money: Is someone claiming to be police or prosecutors and asking for money?
q.app: Are they telling you to install an app?
q.unclear-job: Is it a high-pay job with unclear work?

jobs.title: Wait! This may not be a part-time job
jobs.lead: Saying “I thought it was just a job” does not automatically protect you. Police keep warning international students about this.
jobs.banner: High pay + simple work + hired only by chat + Telegram only → you may be moving scam money.
jobs.ifAlreadyBody: Do not move more money. Do not delete chats or transfer records. Call 112. Reporting quickly can reduce harm.

cash.title: Deliver cash
cash.risk: You may be moving stolen money
cash.why: The cash is often money taken from a scam victim.
cash.refuse: “I don’t do cash-delivery jobs. If this is illegal I will ask the police.”

account.title: Give your account
account.risk: Your name is used in a crime
account.why: Lending a bank account can be illegal. Scam money in your account can freeze it.
account.refuse: “I cannot lend my account. That is illegal in Korea.”

card.title: Hand over a card
card.why: A card is the same as your account. If someone else uses it, you can be investigated.
card.refuse: “I never give my card or PIN to anyone.”

phone.title: Open a phone line
phone.risk: The phone can be used for scams
phone.why: A phone in your name used for fraud can make you a suspect.
phone.refuse: “I will not open a phone line and give it to someone else.”

parcel.title: Receive a parcel
parcel.risk: It may be drugs or crime goods
parcel.why: Collecting a parcel you do not know can be treated as drug transport.
parcel.refuse: “I don’t receive parcels for people I don’t know.”

name.title: Give your ID
name.why: Loans, accounts, or phones can be opened in your name.
name.refuse: “My ID and verification codes are only for me.”

coin.title: Buy crypto
coin.why: Buying coins with someone else’s money can be seen as money laundering.
coin.refuse: “I don’t buy crypto with other people’s money.”

remit.title: Send money abroad
remit.why: “Better exchange rate” requests can be illegal money movement.
remit.refuse: “I don’t send other people’s money overseas. Use a bank.”

show.title: Show this to the police
show.lead: If Korean is hard, show the Korean sentence. Use Big Korean or Copy.

phrases.transferred: I transferred money to the scammer.
phrases.cash-delivery: Someone told me to collect cash and deliver it.
phrases.account-request: Someone asked to borrow my bank account or card.
phrases.fake-police: Someone claiming to be police or prosecutors asked for money.
phrases.danger-now: I am in danger now. I need help.
phrases.filmed: I think I was filmed without my consent.
phrases.unknown-parcel: Someone asked me to receive a parcel I do not know.
phrases.malware-app: I installed an app they told me to install.
phrases.need-station: I want to go to the nearest police station.
phrases.embassy: I want to contact my embassy.

report.title: How to get help
report.lead: Keep it simple. If you are in danger or a crime happened, call 112.
report.emergency: If you are in danger or a crime happened
report.emergencyBody: 112 works anywhere in Korea. Foreigners can call it.
how112Steps: Say first if you are in danger, and where you are.
Use short sentences. If you cannot speak Korean, say “English” or “Chinese”.
Ask for an interpreter, or show a sentence from the Show Police screen.
A building name, subway station, or convenience store is enough for location.
report.interpreterBody: The Korean National Police Agency says 112 can connect interpretation. English and Chinese are often available first. Other languages may take longer — showing a Korean sentence is faster.
report.ifSilentBody: Go to the nearest police box (지구대 / 파출소) and show this screen. The Ministry of the Interior and Safety “Emergency Call” app can send picture or text reports. If it is urgent, still call 112.
report.moneySent: If you already sent money, do this now
moneySentSteps: Call your bank’s customer center immediately and ask to freeze the transfer (지급정지).
Also tell the Financial Supervisory Service at 1332 (weekdays).
Do not delete texts, calls, accounts, or app screens. Take screenshots.

c112.name: Police emergency
c112.desc: Crime and danger · 24 hours · ask for an interpreter

c1332.name: Financial Supervisory Service
c1332.desc: Voice phishing and account freeze help (weekdays)

report.appsBody: You can check suspicious numbers on the police anti-scam site counterscam112.go.kr. This page does not list unverified phone numbers.

crimePage.suspect: If you hear this, be suspicious

voice-phishing.title: Voice / messenger phishing
voice-phishing.what: Scammers call, text, or message you as prosecutors, police, a bank, immigration, Chinese public security, or your family. They try to make you send money or install an app. This happens often to international students in Korea.

lines: 📞 “This is the Seoul Central Prosecutors’ Office.”
“Your account was used in a crime.”
“Move your money to a safe account.”
examples.stop: STOP. Real police and prosecutors never ask you to transfer money to a “safe account” by phone.
dont: Do not transfer money
Do not install their app
Do not give passwords or codes
do: Call 112 yourself or call your bank

lines: 📞 “This is public security / the embassy.”
“Your account is tied to money laundering. Transfer to a safe account.”
“Something happened to your family. Do not hang up.”
examples.stop: STOP. Public security, embassies, and immigration do not make you send money by phone.
dont: Do not continue on WeChat or WhatsApp
Do not keep it secret from family
do: Hang up and call your family on another number

lines: 📱 “Your parcel failed. Tap this link.”
“Install this prosecutor safety app.”
🔊 AI voice: “It’s me. I’m in trouble. Send money.”
examples.stop: STOP. Links, fake apps, and AI family voices are tools to steal from you.
dont: Do not tap the text link
Do not install unknown apps
do: Check family voices with a video call or another number

dont: Do not send money to an account given on the phone
Do not install an app they send
Do not read OTP, passwords, or SMS codes
Do not withdraw cash and deliver it
Do not let them control your phone with screen sharing
actions: Call your bank now and ask to freeze the money
Call the Financial Supervisory Service 1332
Call 112
Screenshot texts, calls, and bank screens
If you installed an app, tell 118 and check the phone
voice-phishing.policeTip: Real investigators never move your money by phone. If anything feels wrong, hang up and call 112 yourself.

cash-job.title: High-pay part-time jobs
cash-job.short: Cash pickup can be a crime
cash-job.what: Jobs that look like easy errands for 200,000–300,000 won a day are often moving voice-phishing money. Police repeatedly warn that international students — including Chinese students — join thinking it is a normal job, then get punished.

lines: 💬 Telegram: “Cash-in/cash-out. Remote hiring. 300,000 won a day.”
“Withdraw at an ATM and take it to this address.”
“You only run errands. It is legal.”
examples.stop: STOP. If the work is moving cash, accounts, cards, or crypto, it is not a normal job.
dont: Do not collect and deliver cash
Do not send money to another account
Do not buy crypto for them

lines: 💬 “Just open a card and a phone for us.”
💬 “Lend your account for one day. We’ll pay interest.”
examples.stop: STOP. Making accounts or phones for someone else is illegal.
dont: Do not hand over an account or SIM in your name
do: If you already did, tell the bank and 112 now

dont: Do not take cash or checks to a place they choose
Do not withdraw at an ATM and deliver
Do not forward money that arrived in your account
Do not deliver items, cards, or phones for strangers
Do not send money abroad or buy crypto for them
actions: Stop the work immediately
Keep chats, transfers, and ATM records
Tell 112 the truth. Hiding it can make things worse
If you have not moved money yet, stop now — that helps a lot
cash-job.policeTip: Even if the ad says “legal work,” moving other people’s money can be treated as joining a phishing crime. “I didn’t know” is not an automatic defense.

account-lend.title: Accounts, cards, phones
account-lend.short: Lending them puts your name on a crime
account-lend.what: If you give someone your account, debit card, banking login, phone, SIM, ID, or SMS code, it can be used for fraud, gambling, or drugs. In Korea, transferring or lending a bankbook or card can itself be a crime.
account-lend.question: A friend asks to borrow your account for one day. What then?
account-lend.questionAnswer: Say no. Close friends, seniors, or people from your country are not an exception. If scam money enters that account, your name is in the investigation, the account can be frozen, and future banking can be blocked.

lines: 💬 “Lend me your account for one day. I’m late on rent.”
💬 “I just need your debit card. It won’t hurt your credit.”
💬 “Just tell me the SMS code. I’ll handle it.”
examples.stop: STOP. “Just one day,” “we’re friends,” or “no payment” still is dangerous.
dont: Do not hand over accounts or cards
Do not read verification codes
Do not lend or sell your account
Do not give a debit card or PIN
Do not open a phone/SIM and hand it over
Do not send photos of your ID
Do not share internet banking logins
actions: If you already lent it, tell the bank and freeze the account/card now
Call 112
Keep the chat that shows who asked and how you handed it over
account-lend.legalLine: Electronic Financial Transactions Act: transferring or lending access tools such as a bankbook or debit card can mean up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to 30 million won. A promise of a loan or a job can still count as payment.
account-lend.policeTip: “It’s my account, so I can lend it” is the most dangerous thought. Crime groups actively look for student accounts.

sns-fraud.title: SNS and online scams
sns-fraud.what: On WeChat, WhatsApp, Telegram, LINE, Instagram, and used-goods apps, scammers offer cheap items, unofficial money exchange, loans, or investments. Chinese students have also had accounts frozen after using unofficial exchangers for tuition.

lines: 💬 WeChat: “Better rate than the bank. Send KRW, I’ll give RMB.”
💬 “Concert tickets cheaper than face value. Pay first.”
💬 “Group buy. Send money, I’ll purchase.”
examples.stop: STOP. Pay-first and never showing the item is a classic scam.
dont: Do not send full payment before meeting
Do not give tuition money to a private exchanger
do: Use your school or bank for exchange and tuition
For used goods, meet in person or use safe payment

lines: 💬 Telegram: “Loan with no job. Pay a fee first.”
💬 “Join this investment room. Guaranteed daily profit.”
examples.stop: STOP. Upfront-fee loans and guaranteed-profit rooms are illegal or scams.
dont: Do not send an upfront fee
Do not invest on a site they send
do: Save the chat and contact 112 or 1332

dont: Do not send large money before seeing the item or room
Do not exchange tuition through a WeChat/WhatsApp person
Do not prepay only for tickets or game items
Do not trust Telegram investment rooms
actions: If you paid, freeze with the bank and call 112
Capture the account, chat, and bank details
Report on the platform too
sns-fraud.policeTip: A “better exchange rate” can be bait to move scam money through a student account. Your account may then be frozen, blocking tuition and living costs.

romance-scam.title: Romance and investment scams
romance-scam.short: Love first, then money and crypto
romance-scam.what: Someone on SNS or a dating app builds affection, then asks for investment, travel costs, or fees. Police treat this as a financial crime. It looks like love. The goal is your money.
steps: A good-looking profile messages you first on SNS or a dating app
They chat every day and get close fast. They call you “baby” or “honey”
They ask to move to Telegram, WhatsApp, or another app
They say they made money from crypto or stocks and offer to teach you
A small amount looks like it made a profit
They push a large deposit. To withdraw, they demand tax or fees
If you stop paying, they threaten you or disappear
dont: Do not send money to someone you have only met online
Do not join or deposit on an “exchange” they send
Do not pay extra “tax” or “fees” to withdraw
Do not install apps they send
actions: Do not send more money. There is no “last time”
Save chats, profile, wallet addresses, and transfers
Ask the bank to freeze funds and call 112
Do not feel ashamed. This is organized crime
romance-scam.policeTip: If someone you have never met talks about love and then asks for money, treat it as a scam from that moment.

housing-scam.title: Rental housing scams
housing-scam.what: For students, the danger is a room that is far too cheap, “pay today to reserve,” or a contract only on SNS. This is not a law class. It is how to stop before you lose your deposit.

lines: 💬 “This room is 300,000 won a month with a small deposit. Pay today to book.”
💬 “I’m abroad. Just send the deposit first.”
💬 “Skip the agent. Direct deal is cheaper.”
examples.stop: STOP. Sending money before you see the room and the landlord is dangerous.
dont: Do not pay before a contract
Do not pay with no written contract
do: Sign at a licensed real-estate office
Check the landlord’s ID and ownership

dont: Do not send a deposit before viewing the room
Do not contract from photos on KakaoTalk or WeChat only
Do not contract with someone who is not the owner
Do not rush because the price is too good
actions: If you already paid, freeze the transfer and call 112
Capture chats, accounts, and the fake listing
Tell your university international office. The same scam is often repeated
housing-scam.policeTip: A real landlord does not demand a large payment before showing the room. The more urgent they are, the more you should stop.

sexual-crime.title: Sexual crime and stalking
sexual-crime.what: This includes hidden filming, threats to share photos, stalking, dating violence, and sexual threats on SNS. We will not describe this in a shocking way. What matters is what you can do now. The fault is the offender’s, not yours.

lines: You notice a tiny camera or a strange hole in a room, bathroom, or taxi.
After a breakup, someone says they will post photos unless you pay.
You said no, but they keep following you or messaging you.
examples.stop: Do not go alone to confront them. Move to a safe place first.
dont: Do not delete messages
Do not meet the person alone
Do not pay the demanded money
Do not pay because of a threat
Do not delete chats and accounts right away
Do not meet them alone in a risky place
actions: Move to a safe place: a convenience store, a busy street, or a police box
If you are in danger, call 112. If you are hurt, call 119
Screenshot messages, accounts, and transfers. Do not delete them
Note the place and whether CCTV is likely
For counseling call 117. To report, call 112
sexual-crime.policeTip: Hidden filming and stalking are crimes. If Korean is hard, still call 112 and use the Show Police sentences.

drugs.title: Drug crime
drugs.banner: Do not carry or store a package if you do not know what is inside.
drugs.what: Korea punishes drug crime strictly, including cannabis. “It’s OK in Korea,” “it’s a health product,” or “it’s just an errand” can be lies. Even receiving or carrying an unknown parcel can lead to an investigation.

lines: 💬 “Receive my parcel. I’ll pay you.”
💬 “Just hand this bag to someone on the subway.”
🎉 “Take this at the party. You’ll feel good. It’s fine in Korea.”
examples.stop: STOP. If you do not know the contents, do not take it. Cannabis is illegal in Korea.
dont: Do not receive, carry, or store it
Do not take unknown pills or powder
do: If you already have it, do not open it. Call 112

warningSigns: high pay for a simple delivery
they will not say what it is
dont: Do not receive international mail or parcels for a stranger
Do not carry a bag or box if you do not know the contents
Do not take unknown drugs at a party
Do not buy or fetch drugs for someone on SNS
actions: If you already received a suspicious item, do not open it
Tell 112 the facts
Keep the chat with the person who asked you
drugs.policeTip: Drug crime can end your studies and lead to deportation. Even a friend’s request should be refused if you do not know the contents.

embassy.title: Ask your embassy for help
embassy.lead: If a crime is happening in Korea, call 112 before the embassy. Missions can help with passports, detention, family contact, and lawyer information.
embassy.first112: If you are in danger or a crime happened, call 112. An embassy does not replace Korean police.
embassy.can: What your mission can often do
canItems: Help replace a lost or damaged passport
Notify family and visit if you are arrested
Share information about local lawyers and interpreters
Explain how to reach a hospital or police station
cannotItems: They cannot stop a Korean police investigation or trial
They do not pay fines or bail for you
They often cannot pay hotel or living costs
embassy.findOthers: Find other missions on the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs site.

cn.name: Chinese Embassy / 12308 consular protection
cn.help: For Chinese nationals. From Korea you can call China’s 24-hour consular hotline +86-10-12308.
cn.warn: If 12308 calls you first and asks for money or a “safe account,” it is a scam. Hang up and dial the number yourself. In danger in Korea, call 112.

th.name: Royal Thai Embassy in Seoul
th.help: For Thai nationals. Call the Hannam-dong mission for passports and consular protection.

vn.name: Embassy of Vietnam in Seoul
vn.help: For Vietnamese nationals. Call the main number and ask for consular protection.

my.name: Embassy of Malaysia in Seoul
my.help: For Malaysian nationals. Seoul mission plus Malaysia MFA duty numbers.

us.name: U.S. Embassy in Seoul
us.help: For U.S. citizens. Other English-speaking nationals should use their own embassy website.
